description: Marks a thread read or unread, moves it to inbox, archive, spam, trash or sent (only while every message in it is one you sent), sets its status (`open`, `closed`, `archived`), replaces its labels, adds or takes off labels by name (`add_labels`, `remove_labels`) or assigns it to a member (`assignee`). Archiving files the thread in archive, and moving an archived thread anywhere else reopens it. Returns the thread and `previous`: what this call changed, as it stood just before, so sending those values back undoes it.

add_labels.description: Label names to put on the thread, keeping the ones it has (ignoring case, a name it already carries changes nothing). Applied after `labels` and `label_ids` when sent with them. A thread holds up to 50 labels (422 past that).

assignee.description: Assign the thread to a member of the workspace, by email address (any case) or user id (`usr_…`); `null` unassigns it. `me` is the person signed in, in the dashboard or through an app connected by sign-in; a plain API key has no person behind it, so `me` from one is a 422. Someone who is not a member is refused with 422 `assignee_not_member`; `GET /v1/members` lists who can be assigned. Raises `thread.assigned` or `thread.unassigned` when the assignee changes.

folder.description: Move the thread to inbox, archive, spam, trash or sent. archive also sets status "archived", and moving an archived thread anywhere else reopens it. sent works only while every message in the thread is one you sent (422 otherwise). A thread in trash is deleted for good 30 days after it was moved there.

label_ids.description: Label object ids (`lbl_…`). Replaces the thread's labels with those labels' names. Sent together with `labels`, the thread gets both.

labels.description: Label names, up to 50, each at most 64 characters. Replaces the thread's labels. Any such name works; a name that matches a label object picks up its id and colour.

read.description: Mark the thread read (true) or unread (false).

remove_labels.description: Label names to take off the thread, ignoring case; a name it does not carry changes nothing. Applied after `labels` and `label_ids` when sent with them. A name may not be in both `add_labels` and `remove_labels` (422).

status.description: "archived" also files the thread in archive; "open" or "closed" on an archived thread moves it back to the inbox.

name: mails_threads_update
title: Update a thread
